snapshot: Nov 4, 2026, ~1–8 AM ET (state races) and ~12–3 PM ET (House)

summary.value: Nov 4, 2026, ~1–8 AM ET (state races) and ~12–3 PM ET (House)

Democrats flipped the House and Senate on a median district swing of D+14.3 points versus 2024, and the swing was so uniform that a one-parameter model — add the median swing to every district's 2024 margin — calls 96% of decided districts correctly; final polls understated Democrats by about 5 points.

summary.note: avg of Silver Bulletin, DDHQ, RCP, FiftyPlusOne, NBC aggregates

summary.value: The swing was strikingly uniform: across the 253 districts on unchanged lines, demographics explain only about 18% of the variation. The correlations that do exist point the same way — bigger swings where the population is whiter (r = -0.30), where fewer adults hold a bachelor's degree (r = -0.19) and in denser districts (r = +0.19) — while the 2024 presidential margin itself barely predicts the swing (r = -0.05).
